Chairman of the board of [[Bank of China Limited]] (2003–2013) | notable_works = }} '''Xiao Gang''' ({{lang-zh|c=肖钢|p=Xiāo Gāng}}; born 1958 in [[Ji'an]], [[Jiangxi]]) was the chairman of the [[China Securities Regulatory Commission]] from March 2013 until 20 February 2016. He was previously chairman of the board of directors of [[Bank of China Limited]], of the [[Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited]], and deputy governor of the [[People's Bank of China]], the [[central bank]] of the [[People's Republic of China]]. He has been credited for playing a crucial role in the reform of China's banking sector.Tom Mitchell, [https://www.ft.com/content/b7f22020-2603-11e5-bd83-71cb60e8f08c Xiao Gang: chairman of China’s embattled markets regulator], ''Ft.com'', 9 July 2015 ==Biography== Xiao Gang graduated from Hunan Institute of Finance and Economics in 1981. He holds a master's degree in International Economic Law from the [[Renmin University of China]] (1996).[https://www.bochk.com/images/upload/ir/p2003-05-28_pdf_e.pdf Xiao Gang (肖鋼)], ''Bochk.com'' Xiao Gang joined the [[People's Bank of China]] in 1981 where he served as director of research, head of the foreign exchange trade center, and assistant governor in October 1996. From October 1998 to March 2003, he was deputy governor of the PBOC, and member of the Currency Policy Committee from 2000 to March 2003. Xiao Gang was appointed the chairman of the board in [[Bank of China Limited]] in March 2003. Xiao Gang was appointed chairman of the [[China Securities Regulatory Commission]] in March 2013.[https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424127887323415304578365820944095466 Beijing Appoints Regulatory Chief], ''Wall Street Journal'' 17 March 2013Ed Zhang, Chen Jia, [http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/cndy/2013-03/20/content_16321778.htm Long road ahead for new CSRC head], ''China Daily'', 20 March 2013 He was the scapegoat for critics after the July–August 2015 stock market mayhem (28% drop in value).[https://www.cnbc.com/2016/01/10/csrc-boss-xiao-gang-criticized-for-chinas-stock-market-mayhem.html CSRC boss Xiao Gang criticized for China's stock market mayhem], ''Cnbc.com'', 10 January 2016 He is blamed for allowing a speculative bubble to grow which led millions of Chinese families to lose their invested savings.Keith Bradsher, [https://www.nytimes.com/2016/02/20/business/dealbook/china-securities-regulatory-commission-xiao-gang-resigns.html Xiao Gang, China’s Top Securities Regulator, Ousted Over Market Tumult], ''Nytimes.com'', 19 February 2016 In an article of ''Foreign policy'', David Wertime argues that the Chinese government, through its state-controlled media outlets, clearly favored Xiao Gang's fast-growth policy.David Wertime, [https://foreignpolicy.com/2015/07/09/china-stock-regulator-csrc-xiao-gang-internet-hate/ Meet the Man Chinese Stock Investors Love to Hate], ''Foreignpolicy.com'', 9 July 2015 On 20 February 2016, Xiao stepped down as chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission.{{cite web|title=China's securities regulator chief Xiao Gang to step down: State media|url=http://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/chinas-securities-regulator-head-xiao-gang-to-step-down-state-media|website=The Straits Times|access-date=20 February 2016}} He is a Non-Resident Senior Fellow at the [[China Finance 40 Forum]] (CF40).{{cite web |url=http://www.cf40.com/en/number_detail/10962.html |website=CF40 |title=XIAO Gang, CF40 Non-Resident Senior Fellow}} ==Family== Xiao Gang is married to Wu Touhong (b. 1959). Wu Touhong graduated from Hunan Institute of Finance and Economics, and served at China Minsheng Banking Corp., Ltd.(CMBC) as chief financial officer. Together they have two sons, Xiao Haojie (Michael) and Xiao Nan (Leo). Xiao Haojie (Michael) served as the board member at [[GF Securities]]. Xiao Nan (Leo) studied MBA at UCLA Anderson School of Management. Xiao Gang has famously let his hair go grey, while most Chinese high-ranking officials dye their hair black.{{cite web|last1=Wei|first1=Lingling|title=The Man Tasked With Stopping China's Stock Selloff|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/the-man-tasked-with-stopping-chinas-stock-selloff-1436349694|website=Wall Street Journal|access-date=14 October 2015}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Bank of China}} {{Chairmen of the China Securities Regulatory Commission}} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Xiao, Gang}} [[Category:1958 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Bank of China people]] [[Category:Chinese bankers]] [[Category:Businesspeople from Changsha]] [[Category:Politicians from Changsha]] [[Category:Chairmen of the China Securities Regulatory Commission]] [[Category:Chinese Communist Party politicians from Hunan]] [[Category:Renmin University of China alumni]]
